Replay

Complete run saves

8 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Converting older Replay runsContent 50 / StormcallerContent 51 / shared turret

Use F5 to save an uncoordinated solo/host run, then resume it in a fresh process with the same identity. Native files and browser slots contain the complete gameplay checkpoint and required spray images. The sections below describe each store and the explicit conversion path for older Replay archives.

Current content 51 adds shared turrets; content 50 added authored pulse attacks and content 49 records takeover timer resets in the simulation. Content 48 made rewind history authority-only in ordinary replication; complete saves retain it. Content 47 added receipt-time dash actions. The explicit offline converter accepts content 42–50 and retains their pending action IDs/ticks, recorded controls and assets. Frozen old action enums prevent the new Dash member from changing the source schema. The control contract explains why the legacy dash control bit remains available for imported history.

Browser solo play saves the complete checkpoint-and-image bundle in IndexedDB. F5 starts an asynchronous write; Saving run… changes to Run saved. only after the database completion receipt. Resume solo waits for the blob and validates identity, content and every image dependency before opening the simulation runtime. The save_run() browser return value means submission accepted; observe completion before treating saved_tick/saved_hash as the new saved point.

Browser records use the profile namespace and reconnect identity. save_slot defaults to run; other slots stay under a separate run/ key prefix so they cannot collide with profile or spray records. Slots are separate from native RSY_SAVE paths. Replacement compares the last observed storage revision. A conflict preserves the stored record and previous success receipt. Reload or use another slot before deciding to replace competing work; no automatic rebase occurs.

Resume uses the bundled image even if the user's separately stored spray preference changed afterward. That preference applies to fresh runs; an explicit selection can still change a resumed run. This rule also applies on native.

web_save_run.sh uploads image A, saves active zone/lob combat, stores preference B, and kills Chrome. It deletes both uploads, checks that a fresh run uses B, then checks exact restore with A and new gunfire after the saved lob lands. It repeats resume after deleting the separate spray record. Stale-save conflicts, missing images, wrong identities and corruption preserve the source save. A slot named profile must preserve the profile and default run. The verified browser path is solo on local Chrome; Room worlds recover through leases/migration. Browser eviction/deletion and the storage contract apply.

On native, F5 writes the current uncoordinated solo/host authority checkpoint to user://run.replay. The menu's Resume solo opens it with the same local identity. A host can explicitly resume a saved co-op run with:

Shell
RSY_ROLE=host RSY_RESUME=1 nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/play.sh
# For a save created in epoch one, other processes join the resumed epoch two:
RSY_ROLE=client RSY_EPOCH=2 nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/play.sh

RSY_SAVE overrides the file location. Start a fresh process to resume; this does not replace a live Session. Clients reconnect using their original tokens, which resolve the saved seats. Uncoordinated clients/observers must be given the resumed epoch with RSY_EPOCH; their default is one. Room handles this discovery and redirect automatically. This manual co-op resume path still needs integrated connection UX. Without a matching local token a player-hosted resume fails. A dedicated server may use seat zero. The archive must match current content and schema; this experiment does not silently convert old versions.

The save bundle contains the checkpoint and all PNG payloads referenced by its players. The checkpoint contains the entire simulation frame, roster, ownership, admitted action frontiers and configured runner state. Zones, airborne deliveries, cooldowns, effect credit, pools, history, run timers and progression resume together. The installed frame is checked against the decoded frame before simulation advances. The new process uses a newer epoch; pending old work follows the standard explicit retirement policy. No fresh gameplay event is synthesized merely by loading a frame.

The file uses the shared bounded codec and staged storage writer. A malformed, wrong-identity or wrong-content save fails without replacing the source. Successful close/rename is a process-crash boundary; portable power-loss durability is not claimed. Saves restore the older world, including its economy, and subsequent local profile writes reflect that restored authority. Profiles are local co-op progress, not an independently authoritative bank.

Room sessions use coordinator-approved prepared checkpoints and migration. This manual entry point rejects Room archives requiring a permit: a local file does not authorize a new leader. Manually restarting an uncoordinated host also requires the previous authority to have stopped; use Room for live handoff/partition fencing.

save_run.sh creates active combat, saves, kills the source process, and starts a fresh one. It checks the actual installed world hash/tick, epoch and seat, lets the saved lob land once, then exercises new gunfire. It also rejects an unrelated token and a corrupted archive while preserving the corrupted file. The scenario uses the same long-lived combat fixture as the Room test.

save_coop_run.sh saves after both players have used abilities, kills all three game processes, restores the host and rejoins fresh client/observer processes. It preserves seats/loadouts and the client's previous cast, permits its next cast, continues saved effects and compares the complete world across all peers. The fixture supplies the explicit resumed epoch. Faulted/repeated manual save-rejoin, connection UX and conversion of older game schemas remain additional acceptance work.

save_assets_run.sh saves a spray supplied by a client, kills all game processes, deletes the original PNG and restarts only the host. The host must restore the image and placement from the bundle before any peer connects. A fresh observer then receives that image, the saved lob lands, new gunfire succeeds and both processes compare their complete world. A correctly framed bundle whose checkpoint still references a removed image is rejected without modifying the good file.

The reader also accepts current-compatible plain checkpoint files when no external assets are required. Older gameplay/schema versions still need explicit conversion. Only current-frame dependencies are bundled: the default resume policy retires pending old actions. A different pending-action policy must include their asset dependencies too. See the bundle contract.

Converting older Replay runs#

The standalone Odin tool converts protocol-6 or protocol-7 / checkpoint-4 saves from Scrapyard content 0x5253435241503042, plus protocol-7 contents ...3043 through ...304a, into current content ...304b. It uses frozen original world/Flash and action/event contracts and preserves existing world values and the control schema while updating the world, action and timing contracts for Arc paths and receipt-time dash. Content-42 actions receive a zeroed development payload. Archived event histories do not exist, so the new event detail, wall-contact kind and arc kind change the contract without inventing past occurrences or spread hops. The converter seeds authority_epoch from the validated checkpoint epoch while preserving the original timer values. Restore installs that exact converted frame; the first committed tick of the new epoch rearms the original takeover timers. See succession behavior.

The normal game loader remains strict. Build and invoke from the repository root:

Shell
nix develop --command odin build examples/replay_scrapyard/tools/upgrade_run \
  -collection:godot=. -out:/tmp/replay-upgrade-run
/tmp/replay-upgrade-run /path/to/old-run.replay /path/to/new-run.replay \
  --identity-file /path/to/replay_identity

Use the filesystem path of this Replay project's 16-byte replay_identity, not a user:// URI. For a test save created with RSY_TOKEN, supply --token SAME_LABEL instead. The identity must resolve to a playable reservation in the archive. Identity verification here prevents accidental selection of another local save; local archives are not a secure competitive progression ledger.

The tool validates the old contract, the full archive and bundle, matching container metadata, complete current-frame image dependencies and bounded PNG header information. It updates schema/content/protocol/contract stamps, maps any pending original actions into the new shape, and rebuilds container checksums. Godot performs the full PNG decode during normal resume. The world, roster, action sequences/refusal reasons, image bytes, tick and old epoch remain intact. Raw checkpoints are supported only when their worlds have no external image dependencies.

The output path must be new. The tool stages and syncs a complete file in the same directory, then publishes it using a hard link that cannot replace an existing file or symlink. A failed conversion leaves the source and any existing destination untouched. Concurrent writers cannot replace the winner. Filesystems without hard links fail explicitly; portable power-loss durability of directory changes is not claimed. No interactive confirmation or in-place overwrite mode is needed.

Resume the output with the same identity and RSY_SAVE=/path/to/new-run.replay. Normal resume advances the epoch and applies its existing pending-action retirement policy. Stop the old uncoordinated authority before resuming its world.

The CLI rejects coordinator-permit archives and custom admission policies; use an application-owned coordinated upgrade/recovery path for those. It does not convert Scrapyard content ...3040/...3041, older layouts or other game schemas. It also does not edit browser IndexedDB records; browser import/export UX remains separate work. See the library conversion contract.

Shell
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_scrapyard/upgrade_run.sh

This gate converts genuine older plain/spray saves from retained protocol-6 and protocol-7 game binaries, resumes them in fresh Godot processes, checks exact frame hashes/ticks and continued combat, and exercises corruption, wrong identity/content, missing dependencies, existing destinations, symlinks and concurrent publication. The original game and original saves remain separate and unchanged.

See authority history for projection, prediction and full-checkpoint guarantees.

Content 50 / Stormcaller#

The Stormcaller revision introduced content 50/J. The offline converter also accepts content 49/I, freezing its catalog shape and adding disabled zero-valued pulse components. Converted runs preserve their catalog; new runs load the current Resources. Network protocol 7 is unchanged, but old peers cannot join the new content/schema contract. See Stormcaller for the feature and tests.

Content 51 / shared turret#

Content 51/K adds the turret pool, authored turret definitions, and targeted mount/release actions. Content-50 imports start with no turrets; new configuration and action-target fields are zero. Existing catalogs and pending action identities remain intact, so this conversion does not inject the new ability into an old run. See shared turret for behavior and recovery tests.
